pr_title: inforschema, executor, util/kvcache, util/statement_summary : Add STATEMENTS_SUMMARY_EVICTED into information_schema
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #23920 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:
- inforschema/tables.go
- executor/inforschema_reader.go
- executor/builder.go
- util/kvcache/simple_lru.go
- Add util/stmtsummary/evicted.go

How it Works:

1. Get evicted digests by editing statementSummaryMap's onEvict function
2. Adding evicted digest elements to corresponding record in `ssMap`'s `other` list.
3. register table to information schema.
### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Tests will be added as soon as possible.

Side effects

- Performance regression
    - Consumes more CPU
    - Consumes more MEM
- Breaking backward compatibility

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->
- fix kvcache, making onEvict usable when quota==0. #24242 
- add information_schema.STATEMENTS_SUMMARY_EVICTED table to tidb.

issue_context.title: Record evicted information of statements_summary
issue_context.body:
## Feature Request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:**

Currently, `statements_summary_history` use LRU cache strategy to cache recent 200 statements and each statement with 24 histories by default. 

The old statements which frequently executed before may be evicted by the new statements. Then we can't see it at some time in the past.

In short, we want to record the following information for a certain period of time:

* evicted_statements_count

**Describe the feature you'd like:**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->

Add a new system table such as: `statements_summary_lost`, query this this will get the following information:

| Begin_time          | End_time            | Evicted_count |
| ------------------- | ------------------- | ------------- |
| 2021-04-08 12:00:00 | 2021-04-08 12:30:00 | 10            |
| 2021-04-08 12:30:00 | 2021-04-08 13:00:00 | 50            |

As, neet provide a related cluster table such as: `cluster_statements_summary_lost`:


Instance | Begin_time | End_time | Evicted_count |
-- | -- | -- | -- |
tidb-0 | 2021-04-08 12:00:00 | 2021-04-08 12:30:00 | 10 | 
tidb-1 | 2021-04-08 12:00:00 | 2021-04-08 12:30:00 | 50 | 


**Describe alternatives you've considered:**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->

related work PR: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/23714

**Teachability, Documentation, Adoption, Migration Strategy:**
<!-- If you can, explain some scenarios how users might use this, situations it would be helpful in. Any API designs, mockups, or diagrams are also helpful. -->

I will provide a detailed design doc later ...

I'll look at the design docs tomorrow and hopefully build a preview version over the weekend

The historical MySQL way to do this would be to implement a status counter. i.e. `SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE 'statements_summary_evicted_count'`. Unfortunately this would not map to the time windows nicely, so you would have to poll this statistic to keep track.

> The historical MySQL way to do this would be to implement a status counter. i.e. `SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE 'statements_summary_evicted_count'`. Unfortunately this would not map to the time windows nicely, so you would have to poll this statistic to keep track.

Yes, so I prefer providing a system table to display this information. 
What do you think of this idea? 
If so, can the table name be called `statements_summary_evicted_count` or `statements_summary_lost `.  Since MySQL uses the name `lost`. https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/performance-schema-status-variables.html#statvar_Performance_schema_digest_lost
I like the idea of copying MySQL. statements_summary is similar to performance_schema, but we have renamed it because it is not exactly the same.
